outputs.text: Nous avons reçu les résultats hier. Toutefois, les données sont encore incomplètes. Par conséquent, nous attendrons vendredi avant de conclure.

The pilot paused because the test account expired. We actually finished the migration on Monday, despite an earlier estimate of Wednesday.

Replaced “due to the fact that” with “because”; everything else is unchanged.

- Priya: renew the certificate by October 6 at 10 a.m. UTC.

The pricing page needs a final accessibility review before launch. The launch coordinator, accessibility reviewer, and review deadline remain unassigned.

Assign a coordinator and reviewer, and set the review deadline. Nia has approved the prices; she has not agreed to coordinate the launch or perform the review.

Practice cleaning a messy sales table in a live spreadsheet workshop on October 12, from 1 to 2 p.m. UTC. The $20 fee includes a practice workbook.

Register for the October 12 workshop.

Among the three tested configurations, Cedar ranked first in throughput at 120 requests per second, Birch second at 95, and Ash third at 80; these measurements describe throughput, not latency. Cedar ran from 09:00 to 09:30 UTC and Birch from 09:15 to 09:45 UTC, overlapping for 15 minutes; Ash ran from 10:00 to 10:30 UTC.

Wait to release until the staging signing certificate is renewed and the export checks pass. The certificate has expired, and no passing checks with a renewed certificate are available yet; last week’s demo used the same export format but does not establish readiness under a renewed certificate.

Priya owns renewal by October 6 at 10 a.m. UTC. Luis then owns rerunning the checks by noon UTC, and Mei owns the release decision by 2 p.m. UTC. These deadlines support the October 7 customer pilot. Proceed only after renewal and passing checks, with Mei’s approval.
Access will be restored by Friday noon UTC only if you complete identity verification by Thursday 5 p.m. UTC. If you cannot meet that deadline, contact support for a revised restoration estimate.
